subject.title: fix: persist pending followup queues across gateway restart

question: Should OpenClaw advance restart followup recovery through a SQLite-backed design and treat this JSON-sidecar branch as source context only, or intentionally sponsor this branch's sidecar/replay approach?
rationale: The remaining blocker is an ownership and storage-boundary decision with security and delivery semantics, not a narrow mechanical repair that automation can safely choose.

options.title: Advance SQLite recovery
options.body: Use the SQLite-backed candidate or a successor as the landing path, after rebase, complete context persistence, and exact-current-head real transport proof.

options.title: Sponsor this branch deliberately
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept the JSON sidecar, trusted replay, duplicate-replay, and stale-drop risks, but that needs an architecture decision before merge.

options.title: Pause behind broader queue API work
options.body: Wait for a broader followup/runtime API direction if durable restart recovery should be solved through that owner boundary first.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite recovery
recommendation.body: Use the SQLite-backed candidate or a successor as the landing path, after rebase, complete context persistence, and exact-current-head real transport proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision turns on runtime state storage and migration ownership, where recent history points to vincentkoc's restart-sentinel SQLite work.
